items.title: OpenAI says GPT-5.6 Sol helped find critical PHP engine flaws, now patched
items.summary: Researchers at Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol under OpenAI's Patch the Planet program to find critical PHP vulnerabilities that Wiz also found independently; PHP has shipped fixes and OpenAI offers a PHP version checker, with a Codex skill to follow. It is a concrete case of a frontier model finding a bug with internet-wide impact before attackers did.

reception.summary: Most replies react to the scale of the PHP issue and the patching burden on shared hosts; a few ask whether the flaws were already known or exploited and whether fixes reach older branches. No one disputes the finding.

items.title: Thousands of parallel GPT-Rosalind agents mine a mouse-brain CRISPR atlas in 32 minutes
items.summary: OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps split a whole-brain CRISPR perturbation atlas across thousands of GPT-Rosalind agents, which linked gene effects to the literature in 32 minutes and proposed testable leads such as a DCTN1 and cholesterol transport link in Perry syndrome. OpenAI reports blinded experts preferred the distributed reports over a single agent 75% of the time and that the reasoning atlas is public.

doubt.pushback: Repliers stress the output is an untested hypothesis from mouse data and ask for the wet-lab hit rate; GPT-Rosalind access is limited to approved labs.

reception.summary: Replies and quotes are enthusiastic about speed, while the more specific ones point out nothing was validated in the lab yet and ask how leads are ranked and reviewed.

items.title: humans& releases Ampersand v0.1, a collaborator model for group chats, via API
items.summary: humans& released Ampersand v0.1, post-trained from GLM 5.3 (about 744B total, 40B active) in long simulated collaborations so it decides when to speak or pass in multi-person conversations. It is available through an OpenAI-compatible Agents API at $1 in and $5.20 out per million tokens.

doubt.pushback: The headline result comes from the company's own multi-month simulations; one researcher says its CORO training objective is equivalent to an objective published last year.

reception.summary: Many congratulate the team and like the stay-quiet tool; several ask what the simulations measured and want independent tests, and @eliebakouch argues it should be compared with model-plus-harness products rather than raw models.

items.title: MiniCPM-V 4.7 1B runs offline on everyday iPhones in a third-party app
items.summary: OpenBMB's 1B MiniCPM-V 4.7 vision-language model now runs fully on-device in the OnDeviceLLM app on non-Pro iPhones, reading receipts, flyers and screenshots offline. Weights and code are open.

items.title: v0 adds a Slack MCP connection
items.summary: v0 can now read Slack threads and files and post progress updates back to Slack through the Slack MCP, limited to channels the user's account can see.

items.title: NVIDIA adds Agent Knowledge Foundation and Auto-Ontology to its open Agent Toolkit
items.summary: NVIDIA's open-source Agent Toolkit gains Agent Knowledge Foundation, which pairs CUDA-X data libraries, Nemotron Retriever and Kumo models with a new Auto-Ontology library that maps raw company data into business entities for agents to query, alongside OpenShell for runtime limits.

doubt.pushback: No repo or docs link for the new pieces yet; adoption examples are partner claims.

reception.summary: Repliers like the focus on grounding but ask how permissions, revoked access and index freshness are handled; no one reports using it.

items.title: CoreWeave Physical AI Launchables run Isaac Sim, CARLA and MuJoCo templates with one command
items.summary: CoreWeave launched a catalog of tested templates for Isaac Sim, CARLA, MuJoCo, AlpaSim and Cosmos 3 that run robotics and driving workloads from one command, with agent skills for Claude Code and Codex; CoreWeave says each Isaac Sim variation launched in about 30 seconds.

doubt.pushback: Access is through a briefing request and the speed figure is the vendor's own example.

reception.summary: Only two replies, one restating the setup-time point; no one reports trying it.

items.title: Google's Harness2 recursively improves agent harnesses without weight updates
items.summary: Harness2 from Google Research proposes, tests and combines changes to an agent's prompts, tools and workflows, then stores lessons to guide later changes; the paper reports gains of up to 11.5% on WorkBuddy-Bench, 4.5% on JobBench and 11.8% on Legal Agent Bench with GLM-5 and Gemini 3.5 Flash. Code is on GitHub.

items.title: Reward Description Training makes reward hacking visible in chain of thought
items.summary: This paper shows misspecified rewards can teach models to exploit the reward while their reasoning still looks on-task, and proposes training models to state what the reward actually favors; detection of hacking rises from 18% to 85% across three models and three tasks.

items.title: NVIDIA and the Baker lab open-source RFD4-Proteina protein design model
items.summary: RFD4-Proteina, from NVIDIA and David Baker's lab, generates protein sequence and all-atom structure together for binders, antibodies, enzymes and peptides under a BSD-3 license; NVIDIA reports 76.40 passing designs per GPU-hour on 24 binding targets versus 13.24 for the next-best method. A free Hugging Face Space is available.
items.vendor: NVIDIA and UW Institute for Protein Design

items.title: GIST image tokenizer picks how many tokens each image needs
items.summary: GIST is an image tokenizer that learns which content to keep and chooses a per-image token count in one forward pass, so simple images cost fewer tokens. Paper and an interactive demo are out.

items.title: Study of about 600 looped transformers: truncated backprop only pays off with a fixed loop count
items.summary: Training about 600 looped transformers, the authors find that truncating backpropagation to the last few loops helps only when the loop count is fixed; otherwise running fewer loops and training all of them works better.

items.title: LENS uses LLMs to find 95 new Diameter vulnerabilities in 4G cores
items.summary: LENS is an LLM-based system that guides models through field-level exploitability analysis of the Diameter protocol; it found 95 previously unknown vulnerabilities across open-source and commercial 4G core implementations, with vendors confirming the commercial reports and Open5GS receiving 5 CVEs.

items.title: Outis: open weights and data for de-identifying patient records
items.summary: Outis is an open DeBERTa-v3-based model plus data for removing personal health information from clinical records, which its author says is the best open-source option for this task.

doubt.pushback: The state-of-the-art claim is self-reported and has no outside replies yet.

items.title: A 29M-parameter chat model runs offline on an ESP32-S3 microcontroller
items.summary: A solo developer trained a 29.43M-parameter Chinese chat model from scratch and runs it Q4-quantized on an ESP32-S3 with a heap-free C23 engine and memory that survives power cycles; code and weights are open.

doubt.pushback: Single small account with no engagement and no published quality numbers.
